artworks.title: Theseus Slaying the Minotaur (tondo of the Aison Kylix)
artworks.description: Attic red-figure tondo: Theseus drags the slain Minotaur from the labyrinth while Athena stands by — Athens' founding exploit in a single charged cup.

artworks.title: Theseus Victorious over the Minotaur
artworks.description: Pompeian fresco: Theseus stands over the crumpled bull-man as the freed Athenian youths crowd forward — the labyrinth's end painted for a Campanian house.

artworks.title: Bacchus and Ariadne
artworks.description: On Naxos Ariadne turns as Bacchus leaps from his chariot — Theseus' ship already a pale sail, the crown of stars waiting above her head.

artworks.title: Ariadne Abandoned by Theseus
artworks.description: Kauffmann isolates the morning after the thread: Ariadne alone on the shore, the hero's sail gone — Catullus' abandoned heroine for a neoclassical audience.

artworks.title: Theseus Slaying the Minotaur
artworks.description: Barye's bronze coils the hero and the bull-headed beast in one struggle — the labyrinth fight cast as Romantic animal force.

popCulture.title: Minotaur
popCulture.description: The labyrinth's bull-man — Theseus' thread and Ariadne's gift still define how the West imagines the maze.

popCulture.title: Ariadne
popCulture.description: The princess who arms the hero against her brother — then waits on Naxos for a god instead of a king.

popCulture.title: Theseus
popCulture.description: Athens' founder-hero whose Cretan deed — killing the Minotaur — remains his most retold exploit.
